title: Lesson 15 - Sharing Rules: Criteria-Based and Ownership-Based, In Depth
description: Given a scenario, determine how sharing rules can be implemented to share records with specified groups.

questions.question: An org must share all Accounts where Industry = Finance with the Finance Analysts group at Read/Write, keeping OWD Private. Which rule is correct?
options: A criteria-based sharing rule on Industry = Finance targeting the Finance Analysts group
Setting Account OWD to Public Read/Write
questions.explanation: Criteria-based sharing rules grant records matching a field condition to a target group. Ownership-based is for owner-defined sets, and relaxing OWD affects everyone.

questions.question: Which statement about sharing rules is TRUE?
options: They can share records to individual users directly
They only add access for the specified groups and cannot remove access
They apply to all users in the org
They override OWD to remove access
questions.explanation: Sharing rules are additive grants to named groups (roles, groups, territories); they cannot target a single user and cannot remove access.

questions.question: A user must access records owned by two different groups. What is the cleanest sharing-rule design?
options: Two ownership-based rules, one per source group, both granting the user's group access
One criteria rule on Owner = User
questions.explanation: Each ownership-based rule shares one source group's records to the target group; combine multiple rules to aggregate sources. Criteria rules and OWD changes do not express 'owned by specific groups' as cleanly.
